To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ClpP chaperone protease has a unique ability to transfer allosteric signals across the two rings of the proteolytic core and that this property is essential for the function of the ClpAP and the ClpXP proteases.
ClpP rings work independently and that conformational changes in ClpP propagate to the chaperones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of the two most abundant chaperone-proteinases, ClpAP and CPpXP, which are essential for protein degradation and quality control in all bacteria.
the mechanism of ClpAP/ClpXP assembly and its impact on the function of the chaperone-proteinases.
the mechanism of chaperone activation of protease activity in ClpP, which is the first step of the degradation process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ClpA and/or ClpX are able to work independently, whereas ClpP is not.
symmetry in chaperone-protein assemblies is important for the efficiency of their function.
ClpAP and XP are not affected by the symmetry of the associated ClpP particle, and that the symmetry of ClpP is important to ensure efficient proteolysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ClpAP and/or ClpXP complexes can be asymmetric but still functional.

the two-fold symmetry of chaperone assemblies ensures the optimal efficiency of their function by providing two independent chaperone-protein complexes and by ensuring the synchronized activation of chaperone components.

the optimal function of ClpP chaperone-protein complexes is achieved through architectural symmetry, and that this is accomplished through concerted and synchronized conformational changes in the protease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two-fold symmetry is essential for the function of chaperone assemblies.
the two-fold symmetric architecture of chaperone assemblies is not only a structural requirement but also an essential feature of the mechanism of substrate degradation and ATPase activation.
the two-fold symmetry of ClpP plays a critical role in the function of chaperone proteases.
